---
title: "Git workflow"
---

## The model

```
Working directory → Staging area → Local repo → Remote (GitHub)
     (edit)            (add)        (commit)        (push)
                                         ←  (pull)  ←
```

Changes move left to right, one deliberate step at a time, and come back with
`git pull`. The staging area exists so you can commit *some* of your changes — the
finished recode, not the half-written one beside it.

## Clone (and fork, for later)

**Clone** makes a copy on *your computer*. This is what you want today:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/crweber9874/UNM_Workshop.git
cd UNM_Workshop
```

Your edits stay local. You can commit, branch, and break things freely; none of it
touches the original, because pushing is the only operation that would, and you can only
push to repositories you have access to.

**Fork** makes a copy under *your account*, on the GitHub website. That is what you'd
use to contribute to a project you cannot write to — fork, clone your fork, push, open a
pull request. Worth knowing; not needed here.

::: {.note}
[Today you only clone]{.note-head}
The repository is public, so read access is all you need — nobody has to be added to
anything, and nothing you do locally can affect the original. Forking is for the day you
want to send work back somewhere.
:::

## The everyday loop

```bash
git pull                     # pick up changes to the original
git status                   # what changed?
git add R/01_recode.R        # stage specific files (avoid `git add .` blindly)
git commit -m "Recode age into generations"
git diff HEAD~1              # read what you just committed
```

A **commit** is a snapshot of your changes with a unique ID and a message. The message
is for the version of you who, in four months, needs to know why `age_group` has four
categories. Write it for that person.

Every command here works in your own clone with no write access to anything. `push` is
the only one that needs somewhere you can write.

## Branching in your own clone

```bash
git switch -c trying-something     # a branch costs nothing
# ...edit, add, commit...
git switch main                    # back to where you started
git branch -D trying-something     # throw the experiment away
```

This is the whole safety net, and it is entirely local. Let the agent loose on a branch;
if the result is wrong, delete the branch.

## When to use what

| Action | When | Command | Needs access? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Clone** | Reading and running someone's code | `git clone <url>` | no |
| **Pull** | Picking up later changes | `git pull` | no |
| **Branch** | Any change you are not sure of | `git switch -c name-topic` | no |
| **Add** | Choosing what goes in the commit | `git add R/01_recode.R` | no |
| **Commit** | Saving a coherent step locally | `git commit -m "message"` | no |
| **Diff** | Checking what the agent did | `git diff` | no |
| **Fork** | You want to send work back | `gh repo fork <repo> --clone` | your account |
| **Push** | Publishing a branch | `git push -u origin name-topic` | write |
| **Pull request** | Asking for review and a merge | `gh pr create --fill` | write on a fork |

Everything in the "no" rows is all you need today — and all you need to use an agent
safely on any repository, including your own.

::: {.warn}
[Rules of the road]{.warn-head}
Branch per task, never commit on `main` · small commits with clear messages · read the
diff before you commit · never commit data you were not given, passwords, or
`.Renviron`.
:::

## Merge conflicts

```
<<<<<<< HEAD
your version
=======
their version
>>>>>>> main
```

Keep what is right, delete the markers, then `git add` and `git commit`. You can ask the
agent — *"resolve the merge conflict in `R/01_recode.R`, keeping both recodes"* — and
then **read its diff**.

## Undo

| Situation | Command |
|---|---|
| See what you changed | `git diff` |
| Discard edits to a file | `git restore file.R` |
| Unstage | `git restore --staged file.R` |
| Fix the last commit message | `git commit --amend` |
| Undo a commit, keeping the history | `git revert <hash>` |
| Throw away a branch | `git branch -D name-topic` |
| Look at the history | `git log --oneline -10` |

::: {.turn}
[Follow along, if you like]{.turn-head}
Clone the repo, make a branch, let an agent change one line of `R/01_recode.R`, run
`git diff`, then `git restore` it. That is the loop everything else today sits inside.
:::
